Quick answers up front: we can structure a private offer with an initial 12-month committed term and a follow-on annual renewal; Azure supports private offers with staggered invoices via marketplace invoicing but there are constraints around invoice timing and PO line items.

Thanks for the context, Jasmine. A few practical notes from the marketplace team:

- Azure private offers do allow split-term billing but each tranche must be associated with a distinct invoice event. Typical structures we've implemented: 60% upfront at effective date, 40% split as a 6-month invoice (or 2x 20% at 6 and 12 months).
- To keep their consumption and unit economics aligned, we recommend explicit PO line items per SKU and per tranche (e.g., "r-inference-standard: Q1-Q2 300k token units").
- If Chirp needs a short-term uplift clause (right to increase committed capacity mid-term), we can include a predefined uplift band (e.g., up to +30%) that triggers a price tier; note that changes requiring new capacity allocations may need a new private offer or amendment.

I've attached a capacity breakdown that maps their requested uplift to SKU lines and a sample invoice schedule: Chirp_SOW_capacity_breakdown.pdf

Marissa Cole
Marketplace Sales Lead
[Attachment: Chirp_SOW_capacity_breakdown.pdf]
